title: `div` truncates and returns `BIGINT`; `/` on integers is a double division
verdict: `div`: truncate, `BIGINT`; zero divisor raises (ANSI) or NULL; `MIN div -1` raises only at 64 bits
description: `a div b` (`IntegralDivide`) truncates toward zero (`-7 div 2` is -3) and always returns `BIGINT`, whatever the operands' width. So `TINYINT -128 div -1` is 128, `SMALLINT -32768 div -1` 32768 and `INT -2147483648 div -1` 2147483648: no overflow below 64 bits. `BIGINT MIN div -1` raises `ARITHMETIC_OVERFLOW` under ANSI and wraps to `MIN` without it.
A zero divisor raises `DIVIDE_BY_ZERO` under ANSI and gives NULL without it, for `div` and `/`.
`a / b` on integers casts both to `DOUBLE` and divides: `-7 / 2` is -3.5 (spark-implicit-casts).
reference: `divide` on integers truncates toward zero and returns the operands' type, with `on_division_by_zero: ERROR` when the plan omits it (`NULL` when asked) and `overflow: ERROR` at `MIN / -1` at the declared width; `on_domain_error` never applies. Spark's `div` truncates natively and raises on zero under ANSI; at `i8`, `i16`, `i32` its `BIGINT` result needs a cast back, which raises under ANSI where the reference does.

evidence.note: `DivModLike`: a zero divisor is NULL unless `failOnError`, which raises `DIVIDE_BY_ZERO`

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.

evidence.note: `div` of `DECIMAL(38,0)` -9999999999999999999999 by 10^21 is -9, a `bigint`: it truncates toward zero

provenance.notes: Spark's SQL query tests at tag v4.3.0: the golden files under results/ run with ANSI on, those under results/nonansi/ with it off.

notes: `python -m sverify_dev.spark_fuzz --rows 300 --seed 738`: random rows leaning on the fact's edges, each construct run with spark.sql.ansi.enabled on and off, on the folded and the codegen path, and compared with a model of this fact (value, result type, error class). 9594 of 9594 results as the fact says; Spark's value differs from Rel.eval's (sverify's lift, reference profile) on 0 of 1146 rows compared.
